grammar.title: Saying where an action happens: 在 + place + verb
grammar.explanation: In Chinese the place of an action comes BEFORE the verb, inside a 在-phrase. So 'I study Chinese in Taiwan' is 我在台灣學習漢語 — first who, then where, then what they do. English word order (verb first, place last) does not work here.
grammar.contrast: 在 can also be the main verb, meaning 'to be at' (我在學校 = I'm at school). What decides it: if another verb follows 在 + place, 在 marks the location of that action; if nothing follows, 在 itself is the verb.
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English order and put the place after the verb, saying 我學習漢語在台灣. The 在-phrase must come before 學習.

examples.gloss: He goes to school in Beijing.

passage.title: 我學漢語
passage.hanzi: 我叫小文,住在台北,現在在大學讀書。我的同學小明是中國人,他家在北京。我們都喜歡學習漢語。週末我們坐捷運去學校附近的咖啡店,點一杯珍珠奶茶,一起讀書、寫字。他認識的字多,我不認識的字,他都會讀。老師說,天天讀漢語,明年我們都會說得不錯。
passage.gloss: My name is Xiaowen. I live in Taipei and I'm at university now. My classmate Xiaoming is Chinese; his home is in Beijing. We both like studying Chinese. On weekends we take the MRT to a coffee shop near school, order a bubble milk tea, and read and write characters together. He knows a lot of characters — the ones I don't know, he can read. Our teacher says that if we read Chinese every day, next year we'll both speak quite well.

grammar.title: 會 and 能: two kinds of "can"
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 會／能 + 動詞（＋賓語）
grammar.explanation: 會 marks a skill you have learned (speaking a language, riding a bike, cooking) and it is also used for what is likely to happen: 明天會下雨. 能 marks whether the situation lets you do it right now — your body, your time, the weather, or permission. Negate both with 不: 不會 / 不能.
grammar.contrast: 會 vs 能: ask yourself whether the sentence is about a learned skill / a prediction (會) or about circumstances allowing it this time (能). 我不會騎腳踏車 = I never learned. 我今天不能騎腳踏車 = I know how, but today something stops me.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 我今天不會去 when they mean "I can't go today (I'm busy)" — that should be 我今天不能去. The reverse also happens: 我能說中文 for a learned skill, where Taiwanese speakers say 我會說中文.

examples.hanzi: 我會說中文，不會說日語。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì shuō Zhōngwén, bú huì shuō Rìyǔ.
examples.gloss: I can speak Chinese, but I can't speak Japanese.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiǎo tòng, jīntiān bù néng qí chē.
examples.gloss: My foot hurts, so I can't ride today.

examples.hanzi: 明天有颱風，飛機不能飛。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu táifēng, fēijī bù néng fēi.
examples.gloss: There's a typhoon tomorrow, so the planes can't fly.

grammar.title: 怎麼 for asking how
grammar.explanation: 怎麼 goes right before the verb to ask how something is done: 怎麼走 (how to get there), 怎麼寫 (how to write it), 怎麼買 (how to buy it). It can also open a question about a surprising situation: 你怎麼在這裡？
grammar.contrast: 怎麼 + verb asks "how do you do it"; 什麼 asks "what" and takes a noun slot: 你點什麼？ (what are you ordering) vs 這個怎麼點？ (how do you order this).
grammar.common_error: Putting 怎麼 after the verb, like 走怎麼. 怎麼 must come before the verb: 捷運站怎麼走？

examples.gloss: How do you write this character?

passage.title: 我的同學小安
passage.hanzi: 小安是我的同學，我們同班一年了。她會說中文和台語，我不會台語。上個週末，我們騎腳踏車去附近的咖啡店。店裡的小姐認識小安。我不能點咖啡，晚上會睡不好。小安說：「你怎麼不點珍珠奶茶？」
passage.gloss: Xiao An is my classmate; we've been in the same class for a year. She can speak Mandarin and Taiwanese; I can't speak Taiwanese. Last weekend we rode our bikes to a café nearby. The young woman working there knows Xiao An. I can't order coffee — I don't sleep well at night. Xiao An said, "Why don't you order bubble tea?"
